title: Return two keys to an entryway cabinet
instruction: Open the wall-mounted key cabinet. Hang the blue key ring on the left hook and the orange key ring on the right hook as seen from the front. Seat each key blade in the guide directly under its hook. Release both keys and close the door.
context: Returning borrowed keys to their assigned positions in a shared entryway keeps them easy to find. The shallow guides keep the keys steady during door movement.
setup: A wall-mounted painted steel cabinet 360 mm wide and 340 mm high with an oak hinged door, a metal handle, two metal hooks and two rubber-lined guides. The blue and orange plastic-fob keys with steel blades and wire rings start flat on a 260 × 480 mm tray on a wood console. The door starts closed, and two fixed-base YAM arms face the tray. Full dimensions, materials and coordinates are in the README and match the setup screenshot.
scoring: Evaluate all final 20 controls. Each key earns 0.40 if the assigned hook shaft crosses its ring aperture, its position and rotation stay within 3 mm and 1° of the final pose, and gripper contact does not exceed 0.1 N. Award 0.20 extra if both keys qualify and the released door stays within 3° of closed with no more than 0.1 N of gripper contact.
reset_notes: The door starts closed and the keys settle flat on the tray under gravity after each reset.
fidelity: The free key assemblies use compound convex colliders for the ring wires, and enter colliding guides underneath fixed steel hooks. The oak door has a vertical revolute joint. The trial preserves physical finger and cabinet contacts, with each key represented by one rigid ring, fob and blade assembly.
